concerns.message: The literal Rumor flow order (targetedRumorAvailability when the message arrives, then ledger `purchase`, then queue the request for the next `stepIntel`) charges gold before the intel outcome is known, and the ledger has no refund. `stepIntel` can still answer `covered`, `capped`, `none` or `duplicate` for a request that availability rated `rumor`/`sighting`. Its own doc says so (step.ts:212-216): the step crosses a snapshot boundary, or a free trigger of the same (player, type) fires in the same step. One example is a journal rumor of that type going stale on the tick the purchase is processed. Separately, intel request ids are global (`state.requestIds`, step.ts:520-533), but the ledger's are per player. If the room passes the client's raw id, player B's first purchase with an id player A already used is charged by the ledger and answered `duplicate` by intel.
concerns.consequence: A player pays 25 gold and gets no rumor. That breaks §11, intel.md's 'charge only for rumor or sighting' and objectives.md's 'a rumor that cannot be delivered is never bought'. `checkLedger` still passes, because the gold identity holds, so no acceptance test catches it. Counter-style client request ids make the cross-player case easy to hit. Fixing it after the worker has built the flow means reworking the purchase path, its replay cache and its tests.

concerns.message: Acceptance 5 says 'no frame to a player carries another player's id', but the synced state already sends ids to other clients: `ShipSchema.id` for ships in sight, the grapple `attackerId`/`defenderId`, and the results ordered by id. The scripted match has to include a duel for the fresh rumor, so the ships will be in sight.
concerns.consequence: Read literally, the test cannot pass. The worker will narrow it on the fly, maybe too far. It should be scoped explicitly: no rumor, sighting or journal frame, message or status patch, carries an id, rubbing id or hidden position; no frame to player B contains A's rumor text or entries; and nothing sends an id to a player who couldn't already see that ship.

concerns.message: The journal needs more than the intel state keeps. `JournalRumor` holds only island/sector leads. Carrier sightings and `no-lead` are one-shot messages that are never stored, and a replacement isn't linked to the stale entry it replaces. It can even arrive at a later boundary when it's a deferred sighting.
concerns.consequence: 'Greyed out with their replacement' and 'reconnect gets the journal back unchanged' both need a room-owned per-player log: sightings, no-leads, the stale→replacement link by (type, reason replacement, first lead after the stale tick), and the delivered body per (player, request id) for replayed purchases. Without that log, a reconnect loses sightings and the replacement links, and a replayed purchase can't resend its rumor.

concerns.message: Acceptance 4 (sightings) needs every copy of a type carried by others. The slice has 4 copies per type and a player holds at most one per type, so the test needs at least 5 headless players, 4 of whom collect the same type. It also needs a test timing knob for `carrierIntervalTicks`, since the validator requires the delay to equal the interval and the carrier reveal to be a multiple of it. `server.ts` test timings expose only sectors and carriers today.
concerns.consequence: Built naively (sailing, ruins, six-second holds in sequence), this one test can eat much of the 300 s integration budget. It needs `placeShip`, open test ruins and parallel collections.

concerns.message: Tab as a global journal toggle takes over the browser's focus traversal. The journal itself has focusable 'Buy a rumor' buttons, and §13 asks for keyboard-navigable menus.
concerns.consequence: If the handler calls preventDefault on Tab everywhere, keyboard users can't tab to the buy buttons or lobby controls. If it doesn't, Tab moves focus away and the Playwright step may toggle the wrong thing. Settle the rule now: preventDefault only when focus isn't in a form control or button, and buttons are also reachable by click and Enter.

simpler_alternative: Settle the purchase inside the world tick instead of splitting it between message receipt and the next step. When a purchase message arrives, queue {playerId, clientRequestId, type}. On the next world tick, first check the dock and look up the ledger replay (a kept (player, id) resends the stored body or refusal). Then call `stepIntel` as a dry run with the request under the intel id `${playerId}/${requestId}`. It's pure and never writes its input, so the dry run costs nothing. That dry run is the availability check the Rumor flow asks for. Call `purchase` only if the dry run answers `rumor` or `sighting`. If `purchase` returns ok, commit that stepped state and deliver. If `purchase` refuses, or the dry run answers `covered`/`capped`/`none`, re-run `stepIntel` without the request and send the refusal or 'covered'. The draws are keyed per (seed, tick, player, type), so other players' results don't change. The order is still availability, then purchase, then deliver, and it can never charge for an undelivered rumor.
cheap_experiment: A 20-minute vitest against the pure exports, with no room: build an intel state where player P has an active journal rumor for sun at island X, and a view where X's sun source is still sealed. Assert `targetedRumorAvailability(P, sun)` is `rumor`. Then step with a view where another player has collected X's source, passing `[{requestId:'1', playerId:P, type:'sun'}]`, and assert the outcome is `covered` and not `rumor`. In the same file, step a request with id '1' for a second player Q and show it comes back `duplicate`. If both show up, charging at message time has to change before the worker starts. If they don't, the literal order is safe and this P1 can be dropped.
